title: Observational maritime target-trial design validator and confounding-by-indication falsification

owns: baseline covariate timing and leakage checks
coarsened propensity overlap and effective sample size diagnostics

paradigm.per_unit_time_zero: Eligibility, treatment assignment and follow-up start must align within each asset. Different assets may enter at different wall-clock times; forcing one cohort-wide timestamp would be incorrect.
paradigm.observational_boundary: Observational assignment is not randomized. Structural eligibility is not identification; the report never emits an effect estimate.
paradigm.confounding_by_indication: A synthetic oracle demonstrates how a true beneficial repair may appear harmful in crude observational means when baseline severity affects both treatment assignment and outcome.

protocol_requirements: Eligibility rules, target population and analysis plan are digest-bound and preregistered.
Treatment and comparator strategy versions are distinct and explicitly named.
Time zero is defined per unit and aligns eligibility, assignment and follow-up start within the declared tolerance.
Baseline covariates are observed and available before that unit's time zero; post-treatment covariates are rejected.
Every declared baseline covariate is present for each eligible unit.
Each unit belongs to exactly one declared stratum and has one independent unit ID.
Propensity estimates bind the declared propensity model and fit-data digests and must lie within a preregistered support interval.
Each stratum declares minimum repair/comparator counts, minimum coarsened propensity overlap and minimum effective sample size per arm.
The report distinguishes positivity failure from insufficient effective sample size.
Treatment versions must match the strategy arm assigned to each unit.
Concurrent interventions block single-intervention attribution until resolved or explicitly modeled.
Complete follow-up requires a source-bound outcome measured after the declared horizon.
Censoring, preventive replacement, competing events, loss to follow-up and administrative censoring are not relabeled as successful outcomes.
Outcome evidence binds source, method, dependency domain, quality, calibration record, calibration validity interval and absolute uncertainty.
Calibration must be effective by outcome observation and remain valid through evidence availability.
Review references for exchangeability, treatment versions, censoring and interference must be present; missing reviews are explicit not-identified reasons.
The report always states causal_effect_estimated=false and all authorization fields false.
The propensity model's declared fit-covariate IDs must exactly equal the preregistered baseline covariate set; post-treatment variables are not eligible fit inputs.
The propensity support floor and ceiling are preregistered and checked for every unit.
A unit's time zero is per asset; the cohort need not share one absolute timestamp.
A complete-follow-up record cannot simultaneously carry a censoring timestamp; censored/competing records must preserve their censoring time.

The propensity model fit-covariate IDs must exactly equal the declared pre-treatment baseline covariate set; a score may be estimated retrospectively, but post-treatment covariates and outcomes cannot enter the propensity model.

cases.scenario: Complete synthetic cohort with asset-specific aligned time zero, two strategy arms per stratum and valid outcome evidence.
Unadjusted observational difference reverses the sign of the true positive repair effect due to residual confounding by indication.
Treatment assignment time differs from per-unit eligibility time beyond tolerance.
A post-treatment covariate is used as a baseline variable.
One stratum contains no comparator strategy units.
Preventive replacement censors follow-up before the declared horizon.
A controller tune occurs concurrently with the physical repair.
Outcome calibration expires before the outcome evidence becomes available.
All baseline covariates are present and pre-treatment, but asset-specific time zeros differ.
A propensity score lies outside the preregistered support floor/ceiling.
One baseline covariate is missing for an eligible asset.
The intervention version recorded for an asset differs from the preregistered treatment strategy.
The propensity model declares a post-treatment covariate outside the preregistered baseline set.
A treatment strategy label is present but its underlying work-order/strategy record digest is missing.
The target-trial protocol lacks an independent exchangeability review reference.

claim_ceiling: The P0 module validates target-trial design structure under declared metadata and reports not-identified reasons. It does not estimate a causal effect, prove conditional exchangeability, authenticate source evidence, establish censoring exchangeability, identify unmeasured confounding, transport to marine engines, or authorize maintenance/operation.
hard_gates: The input is explicitly an observational target-trial emulation, never a randomized experiment.
Eligibility, assignment and follow-up start align within each unit's per-unit time-zero tolerance.
Different assets may have different wall-clock time-zero values; cohort-wide timestamp equality is not required.
Treatment and comparator strategy versions are distinct, explicit and immutable within the trial.
The analysis plan, eligibility rule, causal graph, propensity model and fit-data set bind SHA-256 digests.
A preregistration reference is present; issuer authenticity and pre-outcome timestamp remain upstream checks.
The propensity model fit-covariate set exactly equals the declared baseline covariate set.
Propensity fit-covariate IDs are non-empty and unique.
Each unit's propensity estimate is finite and lies in the unit interval.
The propensity support floor and ceiling are finite, ordered and strictly inside (0,1).
Propensity estimates outside the preregistered support are not identified.
Each declared baseline covariate is present exactly once for each eligible unit.
Baseline covariate evidence is observed and available before the unit's per-unit time zero.
Post-treatment covariates are rejected as baseline inputs and propensity-model features.
Each unit belongs to one declared stratum and has a unique independent unit ID.
Each stratum declares minimum counts for both treatment strategies.
Each stratum reports coarsened propensity range overlap and effective sample size by arm.
Positivity failure and insufficient effective sample size are separate not-identified reasons.
Recorded strategy version must agree with the assigned treatment arm.
Concurrent interventions block single-repair attribution unless explicitly modeled in a later protocol.
Complete follow-up requires a source-bound outcome after the declared horizon.
Preventive replacement, competing events, loss to follow-up and administrative censoring are not treated as successful outcomes.
Outcome measurements bind metric, unit, source, measurement principle, dependency domain, evidence digest, quality, calibration and uncertainty.
Calibration validity must cover outcome observation through evidence availability.
Review references are required for exchangeability, treatment versions, censoring and interference.
The evaluator never estimates a causal effect and never grants maintenance or operating authority.
Every recorded treatment/comparator strategy version binds a non-empty work-order/strategy record reference and SHA-256 digest.
A complete-follow-up unit cannot also carry a censoring timestamp; censored/competing units must provide an in-window censoring time.
A treatment strategy version mismatch is reported as NOT_IDENTIFIED, with the unit and declared strategy preserved for audit.
Missing exchangeability, treatment-version, censoring or interference review references produce NOT_IDENTIFIED rather than a silent pass.
